Court No. - 69

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36048 of 2023
Applicant :- Tinku

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mrityunjay Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.
List revised.
2. Heard Sri Mrityunjay Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Bare Lal Bind, learned A.G.A. and perused the material on record.
3. Learned A.G.A. submits that he has received instructions in the matter for which time was granted on 18.8.2023.

4. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Tinku seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 324 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 507 IPC r/w Section 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Harduaganj,
Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56513364/
1 District Aligarh.

5. The F.I.R. of the matter was lodged on 22.10.2022 by Amar Singh against the applicant and five other accused persons alleging therein that his daughter Veenesh was married with the applicant on 07.2.2022.
He spent around Rs.9 lakhs in her marriage but the accused persons were not satisfied with the gifts and dowry and used to trouble his daughter for it.
She used to be kept hungry.
There was a demand of Rs.3 lakhs and a motorcycle as dowry from her.
On 13.10.2022 she informed the first informant and her family members that she is pregnant.
On 21.10.2022 he called on the mobile phone of the deceased which was not answered, then after sometimes he came to know that his daughter has been murdered.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is argued that the deceased committed suicide and died which is suggestive from the post mortem report in which the doctor has found single ligature mark on her body and cause of death has been opined as asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.

It is argued that the deceased was mentally seek person and was under treatment of psychiatrist, annexure no. 5 to the affidavit being some prescriptions have been placed before the Court to demonstrate that there was treatment going on of the deceased.

It is argued that trial in the matter has started and is under progress in which the witnesses of fact have been examined in which P.W.-2 to P.W.-5 have not supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile whereas Amar Singh the first informant was examined as P.W.-1 who although in the examination-in-chief supported the prosecution case but later on has given a version of false implication of the applicant.
It is argued that looking to the said fact the applicant deserves to be released on bail.
It is argued that the applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para-13 of the affidavit and is in jail since 23.10.2022.
7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
Marriage of the deceased with the applicant was solemnized on 07.2.2022 and the deceased died on 21.10.2022 which is after about 8 months of marriage.
It is argued that even the post mortem examination report shows that the deceased was having pregnancy.
It is argued that the deceased died within seven years of marriage in her matrimonial house.

It is argued that the trial in the matter has started and is under progress in which witnesses of fact have been examined and as such release of the applicant at this stage is not in the fitness of things.
8. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
The wife of the applicant died in her matrimonial house within seven years of marriage.
The P.W.-1 Amar Singh the first first informant and father of the deceased while being examined in the trial, has supported the prosecution case.
The trial is under progress in which witnesses of fact have been examined.
9. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence no case for bail is made out.
10. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

2 11.

However, since the trial is of the year 2022 and the applicant is the accused, it is provided that the applicant may file an application for expeditious disposal of the trial of the case before the court concerned within two weeks from today, which may as per its load of work, diary and pendency of cases, pass appropriate orders on the same.
(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Naresh  Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56513364/
